facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with a 10-year history of a slowly progressive, asymptomatic cutaneous eruption on his left leg
16-year history of diabetes mellitus that was being treated with metformin
no history of another endocrine disorder or malignant neoplasm
no family history of similar cutaneous findings
Reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules 1 to 10 mm wide were present on the front and back of the left leg from knee to ankle
Removal of the scales caused slight bleeding
Hematological and biochemical test results were unremarkable
compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate in the superficial dermis

concepts.why: The patient's 10-year history of a slowly progressive, asymptomatic cutaneous eruption on his left leg, combined with his 16-year history of diabetes mellitus, suggests a diagnosis of Necrobiosis lipoidica, a skin condition often associated with diabetes.

The presence of reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules on the patient's left leg, which caused slight bleeding upon removal of the scales, is consistent with a diagnosis of Granuloma annulare, a benign skin condition.

The patient's history of a slowly progressive, asymptomatic cutaneous eruption on his left leg, combined with the presence of reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules, suggests a diagnosis of Stasis dermatitis, a skin condition caused by poor circulation.

The patient's 16-year history of diabetes mellitus, combined with the presence of reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules on his left leg, suggests a diagnosis of Diabetic dermopathy, a skin condition often associated with diabetes.

The presence of compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate in the superficial dermis, as seen in the patient's lesional skin biopsy, is consistent with a diagnosis of Lichen planus, a chronic inflammatory skin condition.

The presence of reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules on the patient's left leg, combined with the findings of compact hyperkeratosis and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate in the superficial dermis, suggests a diagnosis of Psoriasis, a chronic inflammatory skin condition.

The presence of reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules on the patient's left leg, which caused slight bleeding upon removal of the scales, is consistent with a diagnosis of Eczema, a chronic inflammatory skin condition.
The presence of reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules on the patient's left leg suggests a diagnosis of Keratosis pilaris, a benign skin condition characterized by rough, dry skin.
